# ESMA's jurisdiction over ESG, and dated status tracker

Checked against the library texts on 23 Oct 2026. Quote the Regulation from `library/text/L1-ESGR.txt`.

## 1. Jurisdiction in one page
| Topic | Position | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Who supervises | ESMA alone authorises, registers, recognises, supervises and sanctions ESG rating providers. National authorities have no licensing role; ESMA may delegate tasks. | Arts 4-12, 29, 32-43 |
| National authorities | Designated by 2 Apr 2026. They monitor regulated financial undertakings' own-rating marketing disclosures. | Art 30; Art 2(2)(c) |
| Territorial reach | "operating in the Union": EU providers that publish or distribute; non-EU providers that distribute to EU financial firms, companies or authorities. | Art 2(1) |
| What is caught | Opinion or score based on "both an established methodology and a defined ranking system", whatever the label. | Art 3(1); Q&A 2853 |
| Limit on ESMA | "shall not interfere with the content of ESG ratings or methodologies" | Art 28 |
| EU route | Authorisation: completeness check 25 working days, decision 90 (or 120); silence = rejection. | Arts 6-8 |
| Small EU providers | Registration; lighter rule set (Art 15(1), (5), (7), 23, 24, 32-37) for up to 3 years. | Art 5 |
| Non-EU routes | **Equivalence** (needs a Commission decision; none yet). **Endorsement** by an EU-authorised group entity (ratings must meet requirements "at least as stringent"). **Recognition**, which is **only for non-EU providers below the small-undertaking turnover ceiling** for 3 years. Large UK and US groups therefore rely on endorsement or an EU-authorised entity. | Arts 10-12 |
| Powers | Information requests, investigations, on-site inspections; can also act against unauthorised operators and those misusing exclusions, and investigate third parties enabling them. | Arts 32-35 |
| Sanctions | Suspend or withdraw, temporary ban, cease order, public notice; **fines up to 10% of annual net turnover, measured on the ultimate parent's consolidated turnover for group members**; **periodic penalties of 3% of average daily turnover, for up to 6 months**; CJEU unlimited review. | Arts 35-41 |
| Users | Third-party distribution is exempt for authorised providers' ratings (Art 2(2)(k)); ESMA's 1 Jul 2026 statement extends this to notified providers until 2 Nov 2026. Financial firms that **issue** their own ratings and use them in marketing must publish and link the Annex III point 1 information. | Art 2(2)(c), (k); Art 49; ESMA statement |
| Transparency to ESAP | From 1 Jan 2028 | Art 14(3) |
| ESMA reporting | Annual report on application and sanctions; annual list of providers with EU market shares. | Art 29(3)-(5) |
| Future scope | Commission review by 2 Jan 2029, including whether ESG **data** providers should be brought in. | Art 52 |

### ESMA's wider ESG perimeter
| Area | ESMA role | Instrument |
|---|---|---|
| ESG rating providers | Direct authorisation, supervision, sanctions | Reg 2024/3005 + delegated acts |
| EU Green Bond external reviewers | Direct registration and supervision (from June 2026) | Reg 2023/2631 (`ADJ-EUGB`) |
| Credit rating agencies (ESG in credit ratings) | Direct supervision; ESG disclosure guidelines | CRA Reg; ESMA33-9-320 (`ADJ-CRA-GL`) |
| Critical and recognised third-country benchmark administrators | Direct supervision; ESG benchmark disclosures | BMR; 2020/1816-1818 |
| SFDR, fund names, greenwashing | Convergence; national authorities supervise | SFDR (`ADJ-SFDR`; SFDR 2.0 in trilogue autumn 2026); fund-names guidelines; greenwashing report |
| CSRD/ESRS reporting | Enforcement guidelines; national enforcers act | GLESI |
| UK providers with EU clients | EU access via Arts 10-12; separate UK FCA regime from 29 Jun 2028 | FCA CP25/34 (`ADJ-FCA-CP2534`) |
